thread.title: Apple Unveils the Xs Max—Its Biggest iPhone Yet

author: Jonathan Swartz
title: Apple Unveils the Xs Max—Its Biggest iPhone Yet
text:
The Apple iPhone XS and XS MAX Photo: Courtesy of Apple By Jonathan Swartz Updated Sept. 12, 2018 3:05 p.m. ET The biggest news out of Apple ’s annual September extravaganza was, well, the biggest iPhone to date—a model with a 6.5-inch screen called the iPhone Xs Max.
It’s also the most expensive iPhone, for $1,099, cementing the company’s recent strategy of raising the average selling price per smartphone.
. “It is the most advanced iPhone we have ever created,” Apple Chief Executive Tim Cook says.
Apple (ticker: AAPL) has struggled to meet Wall Street expectations for iPhone unit shipments in recent quarters, but their average selling price has steadily increased to $739, according to Piper Jaffray and the company.
Another model, iPhone Xs, for $999, comes with a 5.8-inch screen, faster processor and better cameras. It’s being positioned by Apple as a device to take advantage of augmented reality for game playing.
A low-cost version of iPhone X called the iPhone Xr, starting at $749, could supercharge unit shipments with a 6.1-inch, LCD screen, instead of newer OLED technology. It comes in white, black, blue, coral, yellow, and red.
Consumers are willing to pay more for bigger-screen phones, KeyBanc Capital Markets said in a note to clients Sept 4. “Over the last six years, screen size is the lone feature that we believe has demonstrated a consistent ability to drive both volume and pricing power,” KeyBanc Capital Markets analysts wrote.
The trend extends to the next-generation Apple Watch, called Series 4, with screens that more than 30% larger. The watch, starting at $399, includes a snazzy new electrical heart sensor, which allows it to work as an electrocardiogram. Apple has received Food and Drug Administration clearance for the ECG function.
